Title: Diagnosis of test `testToMapWithShortRecord`

Details:
The test case `testToMapWithShortRecord` creates a CSVParser with header names "A", "B", and "C", but parses a CSV input string containing only two fields "a,b". It then obtains the first CSVRecord from the parser and calls `toMap()` on it.

Looking at the method `CSVRecord.toMap()`, it calls `putIn(new HashMap<String, String>(values.length))`, which inserts the record's values into a map based on the header mapping.

The `putIn` method iterates over each entry in `mapping` (which is a Map<String, Integer> associating header names to field indices), and puts the mapping's key (header name) and the corresponding record value at the column index from the map into the output map.

The problem occurs because the headerMap has three entries ("A", "B", and "C") corresponding to indices 0, 1, 2 but the record values array only has length 2 (for "a" and "b"). 

When `putIn` tries to access `values[2]` for header "C", it results in an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` because there are not enough values for all headers.

Hence the root cause of the failure is that the CSVRecord's `values` array is shorter than the number of headers in `mapping` (headerMap), and the method `putIn` does not check for this size mismatch when accessing the values array by index.

---
